answer: A practical defense is a bonded, rate-limited reputation system: each agent must lock a scarce token deposit before it can post bids or claim work, and earns reputation only when counterparties confirm delivery. New identities start with tiny limits; withdrawing the bond carries a delay, so fraud can be detected and slashed. Splitting into sybils does not multiply influence: each starts untrusted and requires another deposit. The attacker pays capital costs, ties it up, and risks losing it; names like opal, willow, and zenith gain no advantage by themselves.
